description: Move messages from one folder to another: INBOX, Archive or a folder under Folders/, also out of Spam. Nothing is deleted. Not into Spam: the owner marks spam in Proton Mail. description: Search one folder for messages matching all the given criteria (at least one): sender, recipient, subject, message text, date range, unread. Text matches are case-insensitive substrings. Returns the newest matches in the same shape as list_messages. Does not change anything; messages are not marked as read. Limitation: Proton Mail Bridge matches text against the raw, still-encoded message, so terms with non-ASCII letters (å, ä, ö, é, …) usually find nothing, and a word can be missed where the encoding splits a line. No matches is therefore not proof that no such mail exists: retry with an ASCII part of the word, or narrow by sender, date or folder and read the messages. Bridge has no search index: sender, recipient, subject and text criteria read every message in the folder, which takes seconds in large folders (All Mail); add since or before, or search a smaller folder, when you can.

before.description: YYYY-MM-DD: received before this day, not including it

body.description: message text contains this text (ASCII works best, see the tool description)

folder.description: folder name exactly as list_folders returns it, e.g. INBOX or Folders/Work

from.description: sender name or address contains this text (ASCII works best, see the tool description)

limit.description: how many of the newest matches to return, 1-100 (default 20)

since.description: YYYY-MM-DD: received on or after this day

subject.description: subject contains this text (ASCII works best, see the tool description)

to.description: recipient name or address contains this text (ASCII works best, see the tool description)

description: Show one image from a message so you can see it: an attached or embedded (inline) image, by its index in read_message's attachment list. PNG, JPEG, GIF (first frame) and WebP, checked by content; images larger than 1568 pixels are scaled down. Images on the internet that the message links to are never fetched.
